From here to Vagharshak reigning in Armenia nothing sufficiently certain can be put forward, since tumults held everything and the people rushed into mutual slaughter; which gave the Parthian Arshak easy access into Armenia, and he set his brother Vagharshak over Armenia as king. Moreover, from Bel, killed by the hand of Hayk, to Vagharshak, 1950 or 1942 years are reckoned.

13. After the empire of the Haykian stock was destroyed by Alexander, and after the death of Alexander himself in the twelfth year of his reign, when his empire had been divided among four generals, as we have already said, one of these, Seleucus, held Babylon after Alexander, and besides other nations he also subdued the Parthians in a great war, from which he gained the surname Nicanor. He reigned 31 years. Then Antiochus Soter, his son, 19 years. Then Antiochus Theos, 15 years. In his eleventh year the Parthians threw off obedience to the Macedonians; and among them first reigned that Arshak the Brave, sprung from the race of Abraham, of the line of Keturah, in the city named Bala, 31 years. Then his son Artaxerxes, 46 years; after whom Arshak the Great, 54 years.

14. This Arshak the Great set his brother Vagharshak as king over our Armenia in the twenty-seventh year of Ptolemy Euergetes, and in the fourth year of the hundred and sixty-seventh Olympiad, entrusting to him our regions that face north and west. He, being a man at once brave and prudent, arranged many very useful institutions, conferred governorships and principalities, and devoted effort to setting in right order families, clans, cities, fortresses, villages, soldiers and commanders; which matters must be briefly reviewed.

15. Making a beginning from his own head, he created Bagarat the Jew crowner and knight, granting him this honour, namely that he should place the diadem on the king's head. Further, he chose certain Canaanites to put the gloves on him, and called that clan the Gntuni, perhaps from Gnit, I do not know. He made Maghkhaz, of the stock of Khor the Haykian, guardian of his person; but the clan kept its former name of Maghkhazuni. He ordered Dat, born to Karnik son of Gegham, to be master of the hunts; his son was Varaz, and from his name the clan was called Varazuni. Then he entrusted to Gabagh the care of his provisions, and to Abel the administration of affairs, handing over towns as well. The clans Gabeghean and Abeghean keep their names. He also established the Artsruni, or Artsivuni, and the Gnuni, or Ginuni; and these indeed were of the race of Sennacherib. He also made the Spanduni, who were to have charge of his meat-market; likewise the Havenuni, who were to carry and catch hawks; again the Tsiunakan, who were to keep snow in summer. Next he chose as guards of the palace men from the progeny of the ancient kings, who were expressly named Oslani, whom the Iberians still call Sephetsul. Finally he made second after the king those who were of the race of Asdahages the Mede, whose name is the Muratsean.

16. Now towards the east he established two governorships: Sisakan, and in it the family of Cadmus; and between sunrise and the north he placed as governor Aran, of the stock of Sisak. That region was called Aghuank on account of the gentle manners of its inhabitants. From his stock flows the clan of the Utians, and the principalities of the Gardmanians, the Tsawdians and the Gargarians. Gushar, however, sprung from the stock of Shara, received to possess Kangark and Javakhk, and likewise the principality of the Tashirians and Ashots. Next, facing the Caucasus, he settled a strong people of the race of Mithridates, satrap of Darius, and called it the governorship of the Gugarians. Then in the broad valley of Basean he gave a principality, called the Orduni, to the stock of Haykak. Then he created as western governor a certain Torkʻ of the race of Pasgam, who on account of the grimness of his look was called Angegh; and the name of the province is Angeghtun.

17. Further, in Fourth Armenia he founded the very great governorship of Tsopʻkʻ, and also the other governorships of Apahunikʻ, Manavaz and Bznunikʻ. To Slak, a bold and very brave man (whether he was of the stock of Hayk or sprung from a more ancient race is not sufficiently ascertained), he granted a few men, and ordered him to guard that mountain and to harry the wild goats by hunting; and he called that people the Slkuni. He gave this office also to Mandak, from whom the Mandakuni derive. And having made priests from the descendants of Vahagn, he distinguished that clan with the name of Vahuni. So too the Aravenians and the Arebavenians. Then he made Sharashan, born in the family of Sanasar, great governor of the region that lies between west and south, and entrusted to him the province of Artsn and the Taurus, namely Mount Sim, and all Coele-Syria. In the same province, having found a certain man of Mokʻkʻ, he instituted another governorship, and in the same places he settled the Korduans, the Andzevatsians and the Akeatsians. However, as regards the Rshtuni and the Goghtnians, which are colonies of the Sisakans, whether those provinces were named after the names of men, or the governorships themselves took their names from the names of the provinces, I do not know.

18. Indeed there is no leisure to write out all the excellently ordered institutions of this king, nor likewise those of others who either preceded or followed, whose deeds have been abundantly committed to writing. At present we have pursued only the description of the governorships; if anyone wished to know them, he would have them ready to hand with many other royal ordinances. At last Vagharshak, having reigned twenty-two years, departed this life at Nisibis.
19. His son Arshak followed, 13 years.

Artaxerxes, son of Arshak, 25 years. He, surpassing all in strength, did not allow himself to be second to the king of the Persians; indeed he went so far as to place the king of the Persians in the second rank of dignity, and advancing westward with a countless army he conquered many nations, until he was killed by his own men.

Tigranes his son, 33 years, who, not falling short of his father's bravery, became famous for his deeds; although he again took his seat in the second place of dignity after the Persians. In his time a certain brigand Vaiko was known, from whom the mountain took the name of the Vaikuni.
Artavazdes, son of Tigranes, 2 years.
Arsham, also called Arsham, brother of Tigranes, 20 years, under whom part of the Armenians began to pay tribute to the Romans.

Abgar, son of Arsham, 38 years. In the second year of his reign all the Armenians were made tributaries of the Romans. For, as the evangelist says, an edict went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered; on account of which [they] came into Armenia also. In that very year our Lord and God Jesus Christ was born of the Virgin. Moreover, this was the one hundred and seventeenth year from Vagharshak; the forty-second of Augustus' rule; the thirty-second of Herod the foreigner, king of Jerusalem; and finally the twenty-first of Arsavir, king of the Arsacids, who are also called Pahlavids, that is, of the Persians, in whose twentieth year Abgar had begun to reign among the Armenians.
20. Now from the first Arshak these are reckoned the kings of the Persians:
I. Arshak the Brave, 31 years.
II. Artaxerxes, 46 years.
III. Arshak the Great, brother of Vagharshak, 54 years.
IV. Arshakan, 31 years.
V. Arshanak, 30 years.
VI. Arshes, 20 years.
VII. Arsavir, 46 years.
In his twenty-first year fell the birth of Christ, which was the fourth year of the hundred and ninety-fourth Olympiad.

21. So, as we promised before, we have reached the goal of our account, having come to the manifestation of the Word of God joined with flesh, beginning from the first man created, which is a total of 5198 years according to the Seventy Translators; this sum we shall write out item by item as follows. From Adam to the flood, 2242 years are completed. From the flood to the tower, 525 years. From there to Abraham, 417 years. From the flood to the birth of Abraham, 942 years. From Abraham to Moses and the exodus from Egypt, 505 years. From the exodus to Solomon and the first building of the temple, 480 years. From the first building of the temple to the second, 502 years. From there to the birth of Christ, 518 years; the sum of these rises to 5198 years. Again, from the birth of Christ to Saint Gregory there are 312 years; and from there to the Armenian era, 241 years.

22. And I, O my lord Gregory, endowed with holiness, compelled by your vehement entreaty, have set my slender talent and unskilled hand to constructing this work; and I have tried, in the brief span of this bodily life, to unroll the most beautiful chronography of Saint Eusebius, which, so to speak, I have copied out. Truly, as the rays of the rising sun scatter light on dark places, so altogether this divine treasure rouses the darkened minds of men to know this passing time. Now whoever thoroughly steeps himself in the teachings of the present life also attains knowledge of the higher wisdom, which is truly ineffable and immeasurable, and, as that blessed, skilful and most deserving Evagrius teaches, leads to the worship of God.

Now then, I shall begin from the first year of the birth of Christ, which I shall establish as the principal era, and with very careful labour I shall record the kings of the Romans, the Hebrews, the Persians, and of our nation.
THE SECOND PART OF THE SUMMARY OF THE TIMES OF SAMUEL OF ANI.

John son of Zechariah was preaching in desert places around the river Jordan, and openly announcing to all that the ANOINTED OF GOD was among them. Then Jesus himself, the Anointed of God, was making the beginning of his life-giving and evangelical teaching, and by deeds and words was displaying the power of divine might before the eyes of the onlookers.

Up to this fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar are reckoned: from the temple rebuilt, 548 years; from Solomon and the first building of the temple, 1064 years; from Moses and the exodus from Egypt, 1540 years; from Abraham and Ninus and Semiramis, 2044 years; from the flood, 2976 years; and finally from Adam, 5228 years.

JESUS THE ANOINTED OF GOD, OUR LORD, according to the prophecies written about him, came to the passion in the nineteenth year of Tiberius' reign. Indeed at this same time we find it related word for word in other monuments of the Greeks too, thus: 'The sun was eclipsed, Bithynia was shaken by an earthquake, and the greater part of Nicaea was levelled to the ground.' And these things agree exactly with what happened at the passion of our Life-giver. Phlegon also, who followed the Olympiads from their very beginnings, writes expressly thus in his thirteenth book: 'In the fourth year of the two hundred and third Olympiad there was a great eclipse of the sun, such as no one had observed before; and at the seventh hour of the day so great a night came on that the stars shone in the sky; Bithynia was shaken by a great earthquake, and the greater part of Nicaea was thrown down.' This is what the man cited relates. And this is indeed a great indication of the year in which our Life-giver was crucified, since John too confirms by his testimony in the Gospel that Christ's preaching lasted three years after the fifteenth year of Tiberius. Not far from that time Josephus also relates that during the days of Pentecost a certain rustling and movement was first stirred around the priests, and soon a sudden voice burst from the inner sanctuary of the temple in these words: 'Let us depart from here, let us depart.' Josephus further writes that about that time the governor Pilate had the image of Caesar set up by night in the temple, against the prohibition; which was the cause of a great tumult and sedition of the Jews. From then on a force of the greatest evils seized the Judaean nation.

After the death of Abgar, who had come over to our faith, his kingdom was divided in two. His son Ananun reigned at Edessa, and Sanatruk, the son of his sister, in Greater Armenia. He believed the preaching of Thaddaeus, but soon cast off the faith and killed the apostle and [Abgar's] daughter Sandukht. SANATRUK, 30 years.

At last, in the final destruction of the temple, Titus besieged the Jews, overturned Jerusalem from its foundations, and slaughtered sixty thousand men. Indeed, as Josephus relates, one million two hundred thousand were consumed by famine and sword, and four hundred and twenty thousand were led away into captivity.

The sum of time up to the second year of Vespasian, in which the Jews were wiped out in the final destruction: from the preaching of the Life-giver, 42 years; from the siege under Antiochus, 238 years; from the second building of the temple, 590 years; and finally from the first building, 1103 years.
While Carus fell in Mesopotamia, Numerian likewise perished in Thrace, and Carinus too in battle against Cornacus.

Cornacus was supreme commander of the forces of Khosrov the Great, father of Tiridates; he is said to have prolonged his life to 160 years, with sight, hearing, hair and teeth unimpaired until his death, and likewise youthful bodily strength. He defeated the Caesar Carus, who fell in battle together with his son.

Up to this point we have run on without doubt, guided by the books, of sure authority, of the eminent masters whom we named before. From here, on account of what remains to be added to our treatise, we are tossed by cares and perplexities, because there is disagreement among the later historians, of whom some wrote more, some less, or kept silent altogether. Yet following in the footsteps of the more reliable, let us pursue the truth as far as we can; and first let us align the first year of Tiridates with the second year of Diocletian, according to the opinion of Moses, the historian of the Armenians, not with the ninth or the first, as some others have preferred. Now if you believe that Shapur the Persian reigned 73 years, one must begin from the killing of Khosrov, and then 46 years must be considered contemporary with Tiridates, so that he reigned 27 years while his father Artashir was still alive, and the remaining 46 after his death; and on this reckoning, God willing, we shall arrange our canon as far as the era of the Armenians, preferring the more certain out of very many [accounts]. DIOCLETIAN, 20 years.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiridates, the religious virgins, led by Saint Hripsime, bravely underwent martyrdom in the city of Vagharshapat, and many prodigies were divinely shown to Tiridates and the kingdom of the Armenians. Saint Gregory, brought out of the prison of the pit by a divine visitation, made the beginning of preaching his luminous teaching; then he also restored the wounded to health; at which time the place for founding the holy cathedral was also shown to him by God, as well as [the places] of the other martyrs' shrines.

Soon, at the beginning of the following year, the great Tiridates himself was baptised together with Queen Ashkhen and with his sister Khosrovidukht, and the nobles of the court as well, by the hand, namely, of Saint Gregory, who had then returned from Caesarea with episcopal authority. From that time, roused by royal edicts, many thousands of people throughout the regions of Armenia cast off the pagan rite and flocked of their own accord to the baptism of the sacred font, with those whom Saint Gregory had appointed ministering.

Saint Gregory, having withdrawn to the cave of Mané, would at times visit the region publicly to confirm his flock in the faith. But when Aristakes returned from the Council of Nicaea, he no longer let himself be seen by anyone; and having prolonged his life there for many years, at his death he was at last borne away among the choirs of angels. Shepherds, finding Saint Gregory dead and not recognising the man, buried him in that very place. But at last, many years later, the matter was revealed by divine will to a solitary named Garnik, and the saint's relics were carried to the town of Tordan.
Saint Nerses restored all the orders of the Church well and fittingly. He was born of Athenogenes, grandson of Yusik, who in turn was a grandson of Saint Gregory.

Meruzhan Artsruni, defecting from Arshak and deserting the Christian faith, begged the help of the Persians in order to gain the sceptre of Armenia. So, made commander of the Persian forces, he burst into Armenia and inflicted many disasters on our country, until, in a great battle joined on the plain of Dzirav, he was captured by the great knight Smbat and perished by a cruel punishment.

Mesrop, born in the town of Hatsik in Taron, was brought up and educated in the household of the great Nerses; then he was appointed secretary of the royal court. But at last, scorning worldly honour, he pursued the solitary life and devoted himself to teaching the people by expounding the sacred books; struggling with no small difficulties in this, he formed the plan of devising letters proper to the Armenian language, so that the divine Bible might be translated as accurately as possible. For until then the Armenians had used Persian letter-forms in court affairs, and Greek, and sometimes Syriac, in church affairs.

Here at last the Armenian kingdom of the Arsacids came to an end, and likewise the patriarchate of the line of Saint Gregory. For although Saint Isaac survived another 16 years and shone in our Armenia with his excellent teaching, affairs were nevertheless under impious governors and Persian administrators. In place of King Artashir, Vehmihrshapuh was in charge, and in place of Saint Isaac the malevolent Surmak, who remained one year; then Brkisho, worse than he, three years; after these a certain Samuel, more wicked than both, 7 years. But we shall place their times in the position of an interregnum, so that the order of the canon may not fall into confusion; rather, we shall ascribe [them] to Saint Isaac after his thirty-fifth year, the series being extended up to the beginning of Vardan's governorship. INTERREGNUM, 13 years.
Here ends the history of the Armenians written by Moses.
After the death of Saint Isaac his disciple Joseph occupied his episcopal see for two years, with the approval of Mesrop, who exchanged life for death in that same year.

Here the 553rd year after the birth of Christ was completed, at which time the two-hundred-year cycle of Andrew was also coming to its end. And from here the era of the Armenians at once arose, for this reason. Since the last full moon of the two-hundred-year cycle fell on 25 March, and the beginning had been on 4 April, it could not be carried further, because after 25 March the 13th of April would have had to be set, on which the ninth full moon fell; and so all the feasts, as is agreed, and the reckonings of the calendar were thrown into confusion. Then at last the wise men of that age held an assembly and established the era of the Armenians, so that the paschal feast of the Lord and the rest might be regulated. But when they found over nine years that they did not yet hold a firm enough rule, in the tenth year of the era a certain Eas, endowed with a skilful mind, and the shrewd men of great ability whom he summoned, established by common decision the cycle called the five-hundred-year cycle. This is the origin of the Armenian era, which we shall adopt in these canons in order to present the dates more readily.

In this age certain Syrian vagrants, brought into Armenia to propagate the sect of Nestorius zealously, were expelled with anathema. Some, however, attached themselves to them, and these translated their deceitful books, namely the Cortosacium, the Cyriacosacium, the Vision of Paul, the Penitence of Adam, the Diatheke, the Childhood of the Lord, also the Sebium, the Cluster of Blessing, the open books, and the exposition of the Gospel of Mani. But whoever put faith in these were struck with anathema.

In these days became notorious the appearance of the false prophet of the Saracens, a follower of Cerinthus and the Arians, named Muhammad, of the race of Ishmael, son of Hagar, who had as his teacher a certain solitary named Bahira, of the Arian sect, a dweller in the desert of Sinai; into which place, namely, the Ishmaelites gathered and increased in number from the time when Sarah drove out her maidservant Hagar.

In the reign of Constantine son of Heraclius, Dvin was captured by the Saracens. As a certain historian says, on the feast day of Epiphany twelve thousand people were killed in the church of Saint Sergius, so that the holy altar and the baptismal font overflowed with the blood of the slain; and more than thirty-five thousand people were led away into captivity. Soon the patriarch Nerses gathered the bodies of those who had fallen in this war and had them laid in that same holy church, which he restored.

Now the king of the Ishmaelite nation fixed his seat in that same city; the first, named Chalarthus, of whom the holy Bible had prophesied that the people of Chalartalabius would sate their swords with blood. He died after eight years, and Amaranus succeeded for 12 years. Now that Chalarthus had advanced as far as Damascus, and in Mesopotamia had laid waste the city of Amida with boundless plunder. Then he had sent out three commanders in different directions: into the Greek provinces Jalus, or Joel, who slew seventy thousand Greeks; and into Persia Othman the Amir and Mavia, commander of the forces, who defeated twenty thousand soldiers of Myrdates, and likewise the Armenian commander Musaeus with his horsemen; and so it came about that they gained control of the Armenians, Persians, Syrians, Egyptians, Medes, Parthians and Palestinians.

Now the reason why they attained dominion was this. A certain prince of the region of Damascus, Sergius, was robbing the Ishmaelite merchants of no small property; and Chalarthus, having often protested about these wrongs without his abandoning his ways, at last gathered the foot and horse of his nation and made three attacks on the enemy, and gained possession not only of his own property but also of others'; wherefore, carried also into Armenia, he tried by force to overthrow the religious faith of the inhabitants.

Moreover, the aforesaid king of the Ishmaelites found someone to conspire with him, a man named Muhammad, a leader of the Egyptian merchants. He was moderately versed in the laws of Moses, but devoted to the sect of Arius and Cerinthus, who said that the kingdom of heaven is bodily, that is, that there would be earthly food for the belly in it, and likewise marriage after the resurrection. He also taught laws contrary to one another, namely old and new statutes, devising absurdities and preaching outlandish things, and most shamelessly corrupting that covenant of Abraham in which it was commanded: "Every male among you you shall circumcise on the eighth day" (Gen. 34:15); but he [circumcised] not only males but even, for shame, females, violating the seal of the Lord's covenant. He also decreed that they should wash only with water, perpetually, in a baptismal font; and besides he taught many other absurd, insane and laughable customs of this kind.

When the Saracens had set this Muhammad over themselves as lawgiver, oracle and commander of their forces for 20 years, they conquered Beznunik, Aleovidia and Taron with the utmost destruction. Yet at last, when Muhammad learned that the faithful were resisting his sect, he granted by edict, expressly to the Armenian provinces, leave to follow the Christian rite, and, so to speak, sold them the religion they followed, imposing a tax: namely that each household should pay four coins, three measures of dry goods, a saddle-bag and a haircloth rope. He allowed priests, nobles and horsemen, however, to be exempt from this tribute. And the Saracens, after extending the bounds of their empire and gaining control of everything, began to be called Amiralmumni. Now after the 20 years of Muhammad, Abu Bakr, Othman and Omar ruled for 38 years.

At this time the empire of the Persians too, which was called that of the Sasanids, was brought to an end, after it had lasted 410 years; and the Persian sceptre was taken by the Saracens, who were called Amiralmumni.
THE AMIRALMUMNI OF THE SARACENS.

Muhammad 20 years; Abu Bakr 8 years; Othman 10 years; Omar 20 years; Mavia 22 years; Marwan 1 year; Yazid 3 years; Abd al-Malik 22 years; Walid 4 years; Omar 2 years; Yazid 6 years; Hisham 19 years; Walid 1 year; Marwan 8 years; Abdla 22 years; Abd al-Aziz 3 years; Mahdi 9 years; Musa 10 years; Harun 23 years; Muhammad 5 years; Maimun 27 years; Ibn Meret 9 years; Harun 18 years; Ciaphares 2 years. May their memory be buried in perdition.

At this time the princes of the Armenians were consumed by fire in the city of Nakhichevan; for this reason the series of rulers is broken off here. Now concerning this interval of time the lord John speaks thus in his eloquent and carefully wrought History: "When the dominion of the Hagarenes had wholly prevailed in Armenia, the native nobles of our country came to an end; and if any happened to remain, they lived under a servile yoke and in hiding. Therefore," he says, "in this History the series of our princes suffers a gap." Nevertheless, since the incursions of the enemy ceased in the time of the lord Tiridates, I shall again place the aforesaid princes in the canon.

Mushegh Mamikonian and Samuel, with their households and other distinguished men of the Armenian army, were slain by the Ishmaelites during the days of Easter. In this age flourished Stephen, chief of the priests at the court, a most learned man, highly polished in every philosophical and grammatical discipline, not without the accompaniment of spiritual virtues. Also known were the illustrious teachers of the Armenian provinces, the lords Ephrem, Anastasius and Khachatur, and David surnamed Romanerus, and the great philosopher Stephen of Siunik, a pupil of Moses.

At the time when Ciaphares was the great Amir of the Ishmaelite nation, and Smbat the Confessor likewise the great commander of the Armenians, there came into Armenia, by order of that same Amir, a certain envoy, Abusethus, who at once seized prince Bagarat, bound him in chains and sent him to Ciaphares. But the inhabitants of Mount Taurus, who are now called Sasunians, to exact punishment for what had been done against Bagarat, raised a hastily gathered force, routed Abusethus's troops and killed him.

Finally Bugha, the worst of all, came upon them with a strong army, sent into Armenia by the impious Ciaphares to avenge the killing of Abusethus; he tormented the nation with many calamities and every kind of punishment and slaughter, especially the nobles and the order of horsemen; and those to whom he granted life he urged with blandishments to fall away from Christ and go over to the impiety of his sect. But very many men of brave spirit, putting on the shield and armour of Christ, scorned all the terror of tortures and pains that threatened them from that criminal, for the sake of the goods of the life to come. Among them was Atom, beloved of God, from the province of Alhage, who with his companions endured a great weight of torments and won the most precious crown; and these were about one hundred and fifty, besides those who became martyrs in other provinces, whose feast is appointed for the twenty-fifth day of the month Mehekan. Not a few, however, unable to bear the pain, stained themselves with disgrace; and these, having lost eternal life, did not gain the present one.

So when that wicked and savage Bugha saw that matters were turning out as he wished, he brought the nobles of the country into his power, partly by guile, partly by authority; among them also the great commander of the Armenians, Smbat, surnamed Aplabas, a man truly to be desired by the angels for his true knowledge of Christ, who was also called the Confessor. Then that evil Bugha, hastening his return to the great Amir, carried the rest off with him in chains, but Smbat by deceit and treacherous promises of good things. Meanwhile, since John had departed this life, Zacharias was put in his place in the holy dignity, who in the space of a single day leapt from the priesthood, or rather from the diaconate, to the summit of the patriarchal throne.

Now all who had been carried off by the wicked Bugha were at once shut in prison by order of the supreme tyrant, and unless they cursed the law of Christ they had to die, not without dreadful tortures. And indeed not a few, terrified by bodily death, fell away from the faith; except the renowned Smbat, who, though he confessed Christ steadfastly and openly, nonetheless died his death in chains. Meanwhile a certain prefect, Stephen, surnamed Kon, fearlessly confessing Christ, was given the palm of martyrdom in the three hundred and second year of the Armenian era. Further, the body of the aforesaid Smbat the Confessor was carried by the faithful with great pomp and psalmody to the holy church of Saint Daniel, to the very place where he had once been thrown into the lions' den.

When Smbat was dead, his son Ashot seized the reins of affairs; and he outshone all his forebears, and so commended himself by integrity and kindness that he won the love of all. On account of this excellent fame a certain man named Aly-Armenus was sent by the great Amir with gifts into Armenia, who conferred on Ashot, besides the governorship, the title of prince of princes as well; in this dignity he remained for 30 years, until, on account of his virtue and excellent deeds, he was also adorned with the royal diadem, being proclaimed king by two kings, the Ishmaelite and the Greek, in the last five years of his rule.

This is the place to indicate how the tyranny of the Ishmaelite nation began to decline towards its end. For although the Bagratuni family reigned, not without the consent of the Ishmaelites, the greater part of Armenia was nonetheless at that time, as also now, in their power; yet not under the nod of a single Amir, as had been the custom from the first Muhammad down to Ciaphares and also to his children. For in the times that followed, governors were appointed haphazardly, as each pleased. And this is a sign of a weak and perishing empire, especially if dominion is divided among several, which was now happening to them. For Sanphares ruled in the region of Khorasan; Lavicus Abuthoraphus in the city of Dara; Ises son of Sechus in Palestine; the son of Abldelphus in the province of Telmar; and others elsewhere, giving themselves to tumults, grasped at tyranny against one another. Hence it is that the names of these impious tyrants are in confusion in the chronological Canon. Meanwhile from all sides they sent into our regions malevolent and savage overseers: namely the beastlike Bula; and the most iniquitous Apsinus his son, who had governed earlier, [son] of the wicked Abusigitha; and also the malignant and ruinous Yusuf, brother of Apsinus; then Nesras, surnamed Shercha; then others like them, enemies of Christ, who, up to the dominion of the Amiralmumni of the Scythian nation, which still continues, harassed the borders of our Armenians with constant raids. Their names, we say, since they are not distinctly written in any histories, as far as we have seen, we cannot set out one by one; especially since they are inscribed not in the book of life but in the records of the impious.

Afterwards the Scythians seized the tyranny in this way, as I find written by the great teacher Sarkavag, who speaks thus: "While the Persians and Medes fight each other with alternating fortune down to this day, the Scythian nation (I do not mean the Greek one but the barbarian) is said to have entered their regions in this manner. The kings of that age, whose names are unknown to us (because no one cared to hand down to posterity the records of events and the names of these rulers), having conquered very many nations, at last themselves suffered long defeats at the hands of the Indians, and summoned aid for the war from the aforesaid barbarians with the hope of very great gifts; strengthened by their alliance, they soon defeated the rebel in successful battles. Soon, when war against the same was renewed, they kept away from themselves those barbarians who had been bringing help. And meanwhile the king departed this life. Then the Medes, entering an alliance with these barbarians, drove out the Persians; and so the dominion was strengthened, as some relate, of the Scythians, or rather, as I think, of the Bactrians, who destroyed the kingdoms of many nations in great and murderous wars." In this writing our scholar followed events down to the reign of Malik-Shah, which we shall speak of in its place using the same author; the times, we say, of his father, namely the bloody Alp Arslan, and of his grandfather and forebears, whose names are given as Tughril Beg, Mahmud and Seljuk: for so we once read distinctly in a codex written in his own hand; and if we have access to that codex again, we shall certainly use it for this composition; if not, we shall at all events pass over men who trusted in their own strength and leaned on a vain thing, who are barred from God's inner sanctuary and from the land of the living. But let us, relying on God's mercy, confess his name, who has done this; and let us bear it with an even mind, for he is gentle towards his saints.

Now therefore let us return to the interrupted order of the canons, and, with one series (64) excluded for the reason stated above, let us say joyfully: They have been driven back from your hand; but we are your people and the sheep of your pasture (65).

After the death of lord Ananias, the throne of St Gregory was occupied by lord Vahan, archbishop of Siunia, from the province of Baghk. But when one year of his patriarchate had passed, a controversy was stirred up against him on suspicion of schism. Therefore in the fortress of Ani, in the reign of Ashot son of Abas, many bishops and cross-bearing monks held an assembly, set him aside and cast him from the see, and gave him as successor Stephen, a kinsman of Mashtots, a man beloved of God, a native of Sevan. But Vahan, staying in the province of Vaspurakan and held there as the lawful successor of St Gregory, gave occasion to a ruinous and grave schism: for they vied with each other in throwing all Armenia into turmoil with anathemas and public offences, until by God's will both died in the same year. They were followed by one year of interregnum. Soon, at the command of Ashot, surnamed the Generous, men endowed with integrity and holy bishops assembled and placed on the patriarchal throne the blessed man of God, lord Khachik, brother of lord Ananias the great patriarch, by whose sound and eloquent teaching and holiness of life the mouth of the wicked was stopped (73). STEPHEN, 2 years.
Finally, after Gagik no one of this line (85) was king. For the Greeks ruled for 21 years. Then Alp Arslan took Ani, the metropolis of the Armenians, and overthrew it utterly.

After the death of Smbat, who was also called John, the nobles, gathered with the patriarch lord Peter in the magnificent cathedral church of Ani, metropolis of the Armenians, by unanimous vote set Gagik, nephew of King John through his brother, in the royal dignity of his uncle; but he neglected the pursuits of war, on which empires rest. And yet in these times above all strength needed sharpening, with the Ishmaelites raging, the Scythians making incursions, as we have already said, and the Greeks themselves seething with sedition, because they saw their realm administered at the will of a woman (86). This Gagik, I say, accustomed from his tender years to occupy himself with literary studies, delighted in them also while ruling. When the Greeks perceived this (a nation compounded of frauds), they lured the man to themselves, making use above all of the tricks of our nobles, who, though they had confirmed by oath that his kingdom would be faithfully guarded by them, nevertheless did not keep the Lord's covenant: and these schemes had this outcome, that they themselves and many others perished in inescapable ruin. For the Greeks, having removed the king to an island, sent governors every year; at which time the citizens and nobles of the city of Ani contended in discord and ambition, and accused one another with mutual slanders of injuring the emperor's majesty and of partisanship for the Hagarenes. Indeed the magnates dared to beset the patriarch himself with accusations, and he in turn, compelled by necessity, brought them to judgement. Therefore both sides were turned out of their homes and carried off elsewhere, while meanwhile the common people lived almost lawless, according to their own desire. And this state of public affairs lasted 21 years. When these were over, a fiery whirlwind driven by a southern blast brought a man-eating beast, by whose burnings our nation was destroyed root and branch: indeed the city of Ani too was stormed after a siege of 25 days, and its citizens were cut down by the sword like brushwood, so that the earth ran with blood, and everything was polluted with lusts and rapes. Truly the Lord was angry in his fury, and utterly abhorred his inheritance (87).

Therefore, since the dignity of our kingdom has been destroyed, it must likewise cease in our canon. For although some part of the sceptre remained, namely of those who lived in Cilicia (88) or elsewhere, nevertheless these too, after the destruction of the metropolis, either came of their own accord into the dragon's power or fled to the Greek emperor; and so the enemies took possession of our whole country. Now let us follow the rest in these canons down to our own age: in the first column the Creator clothed in human nature, then the emperors, then the patriarchs, and finally the era (89), beginning from where we left off earlier.

King Diogenes, surrounded by a huge army, attacked the Persians in war, advancing as far as Manzikert, which he also occupied. On learning of this, the tyrant Alp Arslan at once opposed him, and in a great battle Diogenes was defeated and captured. The victor imposed tribute on him and afterwards granted him freedom; but since his nation was no longer willing to obey him, it made Michael son of Ducas its king. Then Michael met Diogenes in battle and came off the victor; and Diogenes, having lost his army, while he was being led by the soldiers to Michael clothed in sackcloth, was deprived of his sight on the way at Michael's order, and died of the intolerable pain of that wound in the year 521 of the era.

In the same year the sentence of the most just Deity flashed out against that swollen and unbridled beast whose name was Alp Arslan. While he panted with horrible roaring for dominion over the world, and while he prepared to spew out the most bitter venom of his soul even upon those whom he had not yet entangled in his claws, the wicked man was suddenly cut off from the earth by the stroke of a sword, and did not see the glory of God. Yet before he breathed out his most foul spirit, he is said to have gazed at his slayer with wonder and amazement; and so, slain, he went down to the underworld with monstrous bitterness and a soul spattered with the slaughter of so many innocent and pious people.

Here I shall keep my promise, that is, I shall follow out the rest of the narrative of this time, which it was necessary to pass over in the earlier place. That divine scholar, then, the doctor Sarkavag, goes on to say: "When the fortunate Malik-Shah, after the death of his father Alp Arslan, was in the glory of empire, the whole conduct of the kingdom enjoyed a most beautiful order. For he was indeed, as his name indicated, King of kings (91). Nor did he imitate the character or ways of his father; rather he displayed pursuits so contrary that he thought nothing had been more unjust, nothing more hostile to peace or to human life at all, than his father's plans and wishes. So, having arranged everything well, and excelling in prudence and fortitude many kings, and certainly all who have appeared within our memory, he strove at nothing more earnestly than to live most justly and to trouble no one with injury or arrogance. He was also endowed with a liberal nature of mind and lofty counsel, and lastly with a bodily stature befitting a king: and there was such gentleness and sweetness of manners in him that he was wonderfully loved. And I for my part consider only a king of this kind to be rich. In a short time he subdued almost the whole world, whereas other kings usually gain so great an empire only after a long time or never. But he made use of benevolence and courtesy more than of force of arms. Now if he gained so much in so short a time, surely, as I judge, not even Europe would have withdrawn from the bounds of his kingdom, had he not departed this life too soon." This is what Sarkavag relates of his life; he ruled 20 years. Presently I shall append what the aforesaid author tells of his death.

In the year 522 of the era, while the tyranny of the Saracens prevailed, Prince Oshin (92) departed from his hereditary domain, named Mayriats Jurk, situated opposite Ganja, accompanied by his brother Halkam, his mother, his wife and other men of the highest nobility, and taking all his goods with him; and entering Cilicia, he claimed for himself from the power of the Saracens the most celebrated fortress of Lampron, at the foot of Mount Taurus, where Tarsus the metropolis also lies.

In the year 525 of the era King Gagik went to Tarsus to Apelgharib, prince of the Armenians and his kinsman; but when he was returning from there, he was attacked by force by Greek princes near Argia and ended his life by the noose. Others, however, say that while given to hunting and by chance asleep he was captured by the Mandalians (93), then taken to the fortress of Candruscoria and killed there. Paralysed by this terror, the remaining princes of the Armenians scattered in flight. Of their number, however, a certain prince, a kinsman of Gagik, named Ruben (94), who held the fortress of the Cositars, on learning of Gagik's death migrated with his whole house to parts of Phrygia and settled in the town of Colmesolum. In these mountains there happened to live many settlers of the Armenian nation; joining them to himself and being sufficiently strengthened, the illustrious Rubenid held the mountain region by arms, and having driven out the Greeks, occupied their towns.

Come now, since in the reign of Malik-Shah the whole world, and Armenia above all, enjoyed peace—Armenia, to which earlier tyrants had for so long held out the deadly cup—I wish to add the words of praise of the aforesaid excellent doctor, who again writes a very elaborate and lengthy discourse, after he has finished the deeds of the living man, narrating his death thus: "In the year 541 of the era the chief minister of Malik-Shah, king of the Persians, was killed; his name was Hasan, and the title of his dignity Vizier Khoja. Twenty-eight days later Malik-Shah himself also died, poisoned, as the report goes, by his wife: a man benevolent and most gentle towards all, and towards Christians almost uniquely so. His death was followed by an incredible upheaval of all nations for four years. For both his brother Tutush and his son Berkyaruq, stirring up wars in these years, overturned every kind of good institution, while neither held the kingdom firmly. Meanwhile blood flowed like torrents, not only of those contending in battle but also of citizens and provincials of every rank, besides other miseries of famine and captivity. Thus indeed prosperity was driven out together with the king's life: to him had belonged the labour of royal cares, while to others, whether nobles or commoners, their fruit and benefit had overflowed, namely security of life, abundance of goods and the warding off of evils. He so loved our nation that he asked for prayers and blessings; for which reason he also summoned the patriarch to court. And would that he had passed over to Christian rites and ways!" The seat of his empire was Isfahan, which is the metropolis of the Persians, and there he ended his life.

The Romans cross through Thrace into Asia, to go and avenge the wrongs done by the Scythians, Persians and Saracens against the Christians. But they suffer very many hardships from the son of Satan, Alexius, king of the Greeks in the city of Constantinople. He attacked them partly with secret, partly with open plots, and even with deadly food; then, when these same men had been entrusted to the sea and to the guidance of his people by a most wicked trick, he cunningly indicated to the barbarians by what means they might be captured. May the Lord one day avenge these things! For this man and likewise his mother, as we have heard from many, were strangers to the Christian rite. The doctor Sarkavag also records this.

The Romans wrest Jerusalem by force from the Saracens, sixty-five thousand of the enemy being slain in the temple, and still more in the city. Lord Vahram was staying in Jerusalem while the city was being taken (90).

Lord Basil, patriarch of the Armenians, died, and his dignity was taken up by Lord Gregory, who sat with great glory on the throne of the see of St Gregory the Illuminator of the Armenians, from whose line it was known that he too was descended. He, abundantly adorned by the grace of God, on account of the integrity and holiness of his ways obtained testimonies of the highest honour not only from men of our own nation but also from foreign kings and princes, and indeed even from kings and pontiffs of the Romans. He also made a journey to the holy city of Jerusalem, and there reverently beheld the holy places in which God, having come down to human nature, became a sharer in the passion of Christ so that he might also become a partaker of his glory. There indeed the Roman nation, mistress of those same places, which they designate by the name of Franks, recognised how great an abundance of divine grace was in our patriarch: for both from the outstanding form and majesty of his body the beauty of his spirit was easily perceived, and also the genuine orthodoxy of his faith, which he expressed clearly and according to the truest canons, and not without graceful eloquence. Wonderfully delighted by these things, the Romans were joined in a bond of the highest love with our patriarch and with the Armenian nation. Thus all things are governed by the providence of God: for the Lord has not cast off his people, as the words of the Psalmist testify.
In the same year of the era in which the patriarch Basil died, the doctor George, surnamed Mełrik (97), was translated by death to the Lord.

Again in the same year the brave Tancred the Roman, who held Antioch and many other cities and provinces besides, an excellent and upright man, was killed by poison by his own patriarch in that same city of Antioch.

Finally, in the same year, during the forty-day fast of holy Easter, on the fourth day of the fifth week, the day on which the stars were once created, there was an eclipse of the sun. GREGORY (98), 53 years.

Weary at last of the incursions, plunders, destructions and slaughters with which the Iberians and Saracens vied in harassing the province of Ani, the inhabitants of the city of Ani and of the region of Shirak, in order to drive this storm away from themselves, resolved to take refuge in the protection of David, king of the Iberians. So a conspiracy was formed against the emir Abulaswar, son of Manuchihr, who had succeeded to the lordship of Ani on his father's death; and King David was received into the city through open gates: and though he entered thus suddenly, no one suffered loss of life. He took Abulaswar captive with his sons and carried him with him into Iberia, and placed him in so pestilential a spot that within a short time the father perished together with two of his children. Meanwhile, when the brave David too had paid his debt to nature, the kingdom of Iberia passed to Demetrius his son, most richly endowed with every merit of youthful training. Then Fadlun, the eldest of Abulaswar's sons, who had long been staying with the great emir in Khorasan, on learning of his father's calamity and the harmful nature of his place of confinement, hastened to make an incursion into our regions, and having defeated the governors of the outskirts, surrounded the metropolis with a siege. Thereafter a cruel famine held a whole year: and when the citizens went out by night to obtain food, the enemy laid ambushes and slaughtered the men, so that the ground was foul with blood and bones, while he sold the women and children. Yet again and again captains, excellent men, came from Iberia, such as that famous and vigorous Ivane, son of Abuleth, who with brave spirit cut down the raiders: and when Fadlun attacked the city with great force, he himself, accompanied by a few, with the help of the citizens, freed the city from danger. Nor should one pass over in silence the manly deed of a certain woman in that struggle, who, standing quite boldly on the walls, drove back the enemy with blows of stones, scorning the arrows with which she was assailed from outside. The woman's name was Caprea [Roe-deer], which suited her swiftness. Nevertheless, since the kingdom of the Iberians was not yet sufficiently established in that city, and hunger and slaughter raged daily, the citizens were forced to transfer the city once more to Fadlun's power, having received an oath from him that he would take no measures against the betrayers of his father and brothers. Although he did not refuse that pact for the present, nonetheless, once matters were settled, he assailed them with various kinds of accusations and punished them. While he reigned there was indeed rest in Armenia from the usual incursions, but both past losses and the weight of taxes and plunder produced among us the utmost poverty and a scarcity of all things, which, increased by additions from that age onward, persists even to our own times.

But the holy patriarch and prelate of the faith, Lord Gregory, because he had made a friendly pact with Abulaswar by which the see would be protected by him, on hearing of the conspiracy of the people of Ani against him, was vehemently angered with the authors of the crime (2).

In this year the nation of the Romans crossed the sea with a countless army by that same Thrace through which the earlier crossing had also been made, which we recorded above at the year 546. These men showed no memory of those troubles which they had once suffered from the son of Belial, Alexius: for they did not perceive the crafty and deceitful wiles of the Greeks, since they thought Alexius an ally in faith and a servant of Christ. For that reason at this time too, forgetful of past evils, they were still more gravely deceived and mocked by his grandson, whose name alludes to Antichrist: since he, though greatly shrinking from the deeds and religion of Emmanuel, was called Manuel (6).

In the year 610 of the era Giorgi, king of the Iberians, took Ani on the thirteenth day of June: soon, at the beginning of August, he routed eighty thousand soldiers of Shah-Armen with seven thousand: a thing we saw with our own eyes, twenty-three thousand [slain] being entered in the records, besides the rest of the multitude that covered our countryside with their corpses. In the following year of the era, 611, on the 21st day of August, Giorgi occupied the city of Dvin, and from there led away sixty thousand people captive, and also destroyed their superstitious shrines. Then in the year 612 of the era the Sultan of Khorasan, advancing with countless forces of armed men to the gates of our Ani, struck the inhabitants with dread: but after the thirtieth day, that most cunning man departed secretly, and having inflicted a great defeat on Giorgi and his forces, withdrew into his kingdom.
